idea-plugin.name: Lombok Builder Linker
idea-plugin.description:
Reconnect what Lombok @Builder disconnects.

A linker resolves the symbol references a compiler leaves dangling. This plugin does the same job inside the editor: it restores the references IntelliJ drops around @Builder, so navigation, Find Usages, and Rename start working where they silently did nothing before.

What breaks today. Every claim below was measured across all 21 documented ways to use @Builder — not inferred:

  • Name strings point nowhere. builderMethodName, buildMethodName, builderClassName, setterPrefix, @Builder.ObtainVia(method) and @Builder.ObtainVia(field) — all six carry no reference. Ctrl+Click reports "Cannot find declaration to go to".
  • ObtainVia breaks code silently. It names a method you wrote by hand, so the IDE shows that method as unused: Rename leaves the string stale and Safe Delete removes it without warning. Nothing fails until toBuilder() runs. This plugin makes the string a real reference, so both refactorings see it.
  • Usages of the annotated constructor or method come back empty. The only caller is the generated build(), which has no source, so Find Usages finds nothing and Code Vision shows "no usages" — even with call sites right there.
  • The declaration goes grey. A constructor or method carrying @Builder is reported as never used.

Placement decides everything. Put @Builder on a class and all of this works. Put it on a constructor — which the Lombok docs recommend once you have written a constructor yourself — or on a static or instance method, and every link above breaks. This plugin closes that gap without touching the class-level case, which already works.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA Community and Ultimate. It reads members the bundled Lombok support already generates and adds references to them, so there is no dependency on Lombok internals; with Lombok support disabled it quietly does nothing.

Source code and issue tracker on GitHub
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.0.0 — First release.
    • All six @Builder name strings carry a reference — builderMethodName, buildMethodName, builderClassName, setterPrefix and both @Builder.ObtainVia forms. Safe Delete and Rename of a member named by ObtainVia now see the string instead of silently breaking it.
    • Ctrl+Click on a name string opens the IDE's own usages popup, listing the call sites of the member that string names.
    • Shift+F6 on a name string renames in place and updates every call site in one undoable step. Renaming setterPrefix rewrites each generated setter with its own name (withName → setName).
    • Usages of a constructor or method carrying @Builder now include the builder call sites, and such declarations are no longer reported as unused.
